title: Multiplication Operators on the Lipschitz Space of an Infinite Graph
summary: The Lipschitz space of an infinite (locally-finite) graph is defined as the set of functions on the vertices of the graph such that the differences of the values between adjacent vertices remain bounded. In this paper we prove that this set is a Banach space when endowed with its natural norm, and we define the little Lipschitz space as the subspace where these differences tend to zero. We consider the multiplication operators on these spaces and characterize their boundedness, compactness and the spectra.
